title: Measures taken to Strengthen Food Testing System in the country
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Measures taken to Strengthen Food Testing System in the country

FSSAI has notified 259 National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food Laboratories for the analysis of appeal samples
Under the SoFTeL scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been structurally upgraded with advanced analytical equipment and 34 specialized microbiology laboratories have been established to detect chemical, heavy metal and biological contaminants
“Food Safety on Wheels” provides the widest outreach for food testing, training and awareness programme, especially in villages, towns and remote areas; Currently, 305 FSWs are deployed across 35 States/UTs
“Magic Box” is a compact and user-friendly kit containing simple, rapid test methods to detect common food adulterants in seven different food commodities
Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test book covers 44 tests that can be performed easily at household level with the help of water and simple solutions like tincture of iodine for various food products
Rapid Analytical Food Testing Kits are advanced, easy to use, portable and handheld devices and don't require any sophisticated equipment or conventional reagents to conduct tests at the field level; 88 RAFT kits have been approved so far

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
31 JUL 2026 2:32PM by PIB Delhi

Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is mandated to lay down science-based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption. The implementation and enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006 is a shared responsibility between the Central and State Governments.

For the safety of the food and food products through testing, FSSAI has notified 259 National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food Laboratories for the analysis of appeal samples.

The SoFTeL scheme i.e. Strengthening of Food Testing System in the Country including provision of Mobile Food Testing Laboratory (MFTL) is an initiative implemented by the FSSAI to upgrade state food laboratories, set up microbiology facilities and deploys mobile food testing vans. Under this scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been structurally upgraded with advanced analytical equipment and 34 specialized microbiology laboratories have been established to detect chemical, heavy metal and biological contaminants. MFTL or “Food Safety on Wheels” (FSW) provides the widest outreach for food testing, training and awareness programme, especially in the villages, towns and remote areas. Currently, 305 FSWs are deployed across 35 States/UTs.

The “Magic Box” is a compact and user-friendly kit containing simple, rapid test methods to detect common food adulterants in seven different food commodities. It aims to identify adulteration in everyday food items such as milk, spices, oils, and grains.

Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test (DART) book covers 44 tests that can be performed easily at household level with the help of water and simple solutions like tincture of iodine for food products like Milk & Milk Products, Oils & Fats, Sugar & Confectionary, Food Grains & its products, Spices & Condiments etc. These tests also include sensory evaluation tests for establishing authentication of food products. DART book depicts the differences between pure and adulterated food product through pictorial representation.

Also, Rapid Analytical Food Testing (RAPID) Kits are advanced, easy to use, portable and handheld devices and don't require any sophisticated equipment or conventional reagents to conduct the tests. So far, 88 RAFT kits have been approved. These kits help to reduce the screening time of the food products at the field level and thereby accelerate surveillance as well as monitoring activities.

The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare,
Shri Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.
